other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 4784, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027

summary: S. 4784, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, establishes policies, organizational structures, funding limits, and authorities for Department of Defense and Department of Energy national security programs. It covers military organization, vessel acquisition, counterterrorism, cyber and artificial intelligence, reporting requirements, and military construction.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to organizational changes, funding limits, transfer authorities, reporting requirements, restrictions on entertainment projects and language training, and new policy directives.
Governed by policies and authorizations set forth in the bill.
affected_groups.group: Department of Energy national security programs

key_provisions: Establishes organizational changes including the Economic Defense Unit and the Under Secretary of Defense for Cyber, Information, and Networks, and renames the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness.
Authorizes general transfer authority up to $6,000,000,000 and places funding limitations on agencies, programs, travel, and support activities.
Prohibits Department of Defense funds from supporting entertainment projects tied to the Chinese government or reducing certain foreign language training programs without a readiness certification.
Sets numerous reporting requirements, plans, strategies, and reviews regarding defense posture, autonomous and unmanned systems, artificial intelligence, and financial audit readiness.
Covers naval vessel acquisition and industrial base policies, counterterrorism provisions, foreign nation assistance and cooperation, and cyber/artificial intelligence provisions.
Authorizes defense-wide and service-specific military construction authorizations, housing standards, land conveyances, energy programs, and Department of Energy national security programs.
missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for total authorizations outside of the $6,000,000,000 general transfer authority are not specified in the notes.
Specific details regarding land conveyances, energy programs, and housing standards are not provided in the source text.
